L-echo-arrive: Now entering Echo Valley. In this town, whatever you say comes back three days later as a promise you have to keep. So why is one kid carrying a fish tank, calling his grandma and drawing pictures all on the same Saturday?
L-echo-catch: But here's the part nobody tells you. The valley doesn't care if you meant it. Every word comes back as a promise. And they all come back on Saturday.
L-echo-end: Say only what you're ready to keep. So… what would the valley echo back to you?
L-echo-reel: This is Rule Road radio, live from Echo Valley, where every word comes back. Here's what our traveler said this week.
L-fallback-arrive: Now entering Tockfield. In this town, when the clocks fall back, the extra hour falls from the sky, and you catch it in a jar. So why does one grandma have 60 hours hidden in jars?
L-fallback-catch: But here's the part nobody tells you. In this town, an hour can only wait 60 years. At 2 a.m. on fall-back night, the oldest jar melts.
L-fallback-end: Someday is a day of the week you never get. Spend the hour now. This weekend your clock gives you one hour back. Who are you spending it on?
L-hum-arrive: Now entering Harmonia. In this town, every door opens to a note. Only your own voice can find it. So why is one kid humming at a locked front door?
L-hum-catch: But here's the part nobody tells you. If you don't use your note, you forget it, and every door in town forgets you. And tonight is your sister's big recital.
L-hum-end: Use your voice, or the doors forget you. So… what note would open your door?
L-hum-reel: This is Rule Road radio, live from Harmonia, where every door has a note. Here's how our traveler sang their way home.
L-whisper-arrive: Now entering Whisperton. In this town, sound has weight. Loud words crack the glass streets. So why is a whole town tiptoeing… and one kid is stuck on a glass bridge with a birthday cake?
L-whisper-catch: But here's the part nobody tells you. Sound doesn't fade here. Every loud word you said today is stacked on the bridge home. And Grandma's party is on the other side.
L-whisper-end: Soft words carry further than loud ones. So… could you cross the glass bridge?
L-whisper-reel: This is Rule Road radio, coming to you very quietly from Whisperton. Tonight, a traveler tried to carry a cake across the glass bridge. Here's the tape.
L1-arrive: Now entering Hushwick. In this town, you only get 10 words a day. So why is one kid saving her words like they're gold?
L1-catch: But here's the part nobody tells you. At 8 p.m., Grandpa calls from far away. He calls every night. You'll want words left for him.
L1-end: Fewer words, chosen well, say the most. So… what would you say with only 10 words?
L1-reel: This is Rule Road radio, live from Hushwick, where you only get ten words a day. Here's how our traveler spent theirs.
L2-arrive: Now entering Saidsville. In this town, whatever you say about someone comes true for one hour. So why did the grumpiest man in town just hand out free lemonade?
L2-catch: But here's the part nobody tells you. It works on you, too. Whatever you say about yourself comes true for one hour.
L2-end: Kind words come true more often than you think. So… what would you say about your best friend?
L3-arrive: Now entering Chargeville. In this town, your phone battery is your energy. At 0%, so are you. So why is one kid bouncing off the walls… and her brother can't get off the couch?
L3-catch: But here's the part nobody tells you. You can't plug yourself in. You only charge off-screen. And your best friend's party is at 6. You need 40% to go.
L3-end: Charge yourself off-screen before you hit zero. So… what's your battery at right now?
L4-arrive: Now entering Petalton. In this town, every time you say sorry, a flower grows in your yard. So why does one yard on Maple Street have nothing but dirt?
L4-catch: But here's the part nobody tells you. Every sorry you don'T say grows thorns. And Grandma is coming tonight. If thorns block the gate, she can't get in.
L4-end: Sorry is a small word. It grows big things. So… who do you owe a sorry?
L5-arrive: Now entering Boomerang Bay. In this town, everything you throw away comes back in a week. So why is one front door blocked by a mountain of junk?
L5-catch: But here's the part nobody tells you. Everything you threw away comes back next week… and if you toss it again, it comes back double. Mom's birthday party is at home on Saturday.
L5-end: Use it up. Fix it. Share it. Waste less. So… what would come back to your door this week?
M-birds-arrive: Now entering Featherton. In this town, every subscription is a tiny bird that eats from your pocket every month. So how did a bird eat a whole paycheck?
M-birds-catch: Here's what nobody tells you: the birds you forget don't leave. They get fat. And you can only send one away if you remember its name. Rent is 800 coins, due Friday.
M-birds-end: The birds you forget get fat. How many subscriptions are you paying for right now?
M-chain-arrive: Now entering Halfnight. In this town, every coin you save doubles at midnight. So why does almost everyone here quit one night too early?
M-chain-catch: Here's what nobody tells you: spend just one, and the whole jar drops back to one. Your house sells in twenty nights, and the price is a million coins. You have one.
M-chain-end: One night made half of it. Most people quit the night before. What would you have done on night nineteen?
M-hours-arrive: Now entering Hourmouth. In this town, nothing costs money. Price tags show hours of your life. So why did one big red chair cost her a whole weekend?
M-hours-catch: Here's what nobody tells you: the tag never says which hours. And Saturday at seven is your dad's sixtieth birthday.
M-hours-end: Everything costs hours. So ask which ones. What did you buy that cost you more hours than it was worth?
M-jobs-arrive: Now entering Tagwick. In this town, a coin with no job gets up and leaves. So why does your sister always have money left?
M-jobs-catch: Here's what nobody tells you: runaway coins never come back. And the first freeze hits on Friday. Your heater is dead, and fixing it costs 80 coins.
M-jobs-end: Money with no job finds the door. If your money had a job, what would it be?
M-monster-arrive: Now entering Duesbury. In this town, every bill you forget turns into a monster. So what ate her front door?
M-monster-catch: Here's what nobody tells you: it grows every single day. And on Friday the thirteenth, every monster in town comes to collect.
M-monster-end: Open it the day it comes. How many unopened envelopes do you have right now?
M-rhyme-arrive: Now entering Rhymeburg. In this town, you can buy anything, but only if your offer rhymes. So why did one kid get a sun hat for half price… just by saying “that”?
M-rhyme-catch: But here's the part nobody tells you. Every shop in town raises its price by one coin each time you don'T rhyme. They've been counting all day. And the bus home costs 10.
M-rhyme-end: Ask for a better deal before you pay. So… what would you rhyme to get a cake for half?
M-rhyme-reel: This is Rule Road radio, live from the Rhymeburg market, where offers have to rhyme. Our traveler went shopping. Listen.
M-shadow-arrive: Now entering Laterton. In this town, every pay later makes your shadow heavier. So why can't she ride the bus?
M-shadow-catch: Here's what nobody tells you: at noon, you feel nothing. The weight shows up at sunset. And in November, the sun sets at five.
M-shadow-end: If you can't pay it at noon, you can't carry it at sunset. How many pay-later plans do you have running right now?
M-shrink-arrive: Now entering Inchwick. In this town, every new thing you buy makes your house one inch smaller. So how did a dog end up with the keys to her house?
M-shrink-catch: Here's what nobody tells you: your stuff doesn't shrink, only the house does. And if you can't stand up inside, the town gives it to whoever can. You're five foot six. Your door is six feet.
M-shrink-end: Your stuff doesn't shrink. Your house does. What's the one thing you bought that you'd give away first?
M1-arrive: Now entering Doubleton. In this town, every coin you save doubles at midnight. So why does one kid here have a heavy jar… and his best friend has nothing?
M1-catch: But here's the part nobody tells you. The jar only doubles if it stays closed all day. Open it, and the magic skips a night.
M1-end: Savings grow best when you leave them alone. So… would you have opened the jar?
M2-arrive: Now entering Greenpenny. In this town, money grows on trees, but only if you water it every day. So why does one tree here sparkle… and the one next door is bare?
M2-catch: But here's the part nobody tells you. Rain doesn't count. The tree only drinks water from your hands.
M2-end: Tiny habits, every single day, grow the biggest trees. So… would you water it in the rain?
M3-arrive: Now entering Yawnmore. In this town, every time you buy something you don't need, you lose an hour of sleep. So why is the kid with the most toys falling asleep in class?
M3-catch: But here's the part nobody tells you. The lost hours come out of tonight. And tomorrow is the big game.
M3-end: Buy what you need. Then sleep easy. So… would you trade an hour of sleep for a keychain?
M4-arrive: Now entering Futureville. In this town, your bank account shows you your future self. So why did the girl at the bank machine just scream?
M4-catch: But here's the part nobody tells you. The screen changes every day… but on your 30th birthday it freezes forever. And your 30th is coming.
M4-end: Small money, saved early, grows into a big future. So… what would your screen show today?
M5-arrive: Now entering Leashville. In this town, borrowed money follows you like a dog. Big loans are big dogs. So why is one guy being chased down Main Street by three dogs?
M5-catch: But here's the part nobody tells you. If you don't pay them back, the dogs keep growing every month. And your big job interview is next week.
M5-end: Borrow small. Pay it back fast. Walk free. So… how many dogs are following you?
M8-arrive: Now entering Tillsbury. In this town, your wallet talks, and it warns you before you spend. So why did one wallet scream in the middle of the mall?
M8-catch: Here's what nobody tells you: hit zero and your wallet falls asleep for a month, right before Black Friday. And your mom's birthday is Black Friday.
M8-end: The best deal is the one you don't need. What's the worst thing you ever bought on sale?
